# Miataru DeviceKey authentication plan (2026-01-31 13:59Z)

_**User**_

Create a plan which covers the following extension of functionality:

The Miataru server and all write requests through the Miataru client supports a DeviceKey. 

DeviceKey authentication provides secure, device-level authentication for location updates and sensitive operations. Each device can set a unique cryptographic key (up to 256 Unicode characters) that must be provided for protected operations.

## First-Time Setup
Device owners set an initial DeviceKey using the /v1/setDeviceKey endpoint

## Key Validation
When a DeviceKey is set, protected endpoints require the key to be provided

## Key Management
DeviceKeys can be changed by providing the current key along with the new key

## Protected Operations
The following operations require DeviceKey authentication when a DeviceKey is set for the device:
- UpdateLocation - Prevents unauthorized location updates
- DeleteLocation - Prevents unauthorized deletion of location data
- GetVisitorHistory - Protects access to visitor tracking data
- SetAllowedDeviceList - Secures access control configuration

## Benefits
- Prevent Unauthorized Updates: Only devices with the correct key can update location data
- Protect Sensitive Data: Visitor history requires authentication
- Secure Configuration: Access control settings are protected

## App-Implementation/Flow:
Initially (when a DeviceID is generated) the DeviceKey is empty and not set. The app should hold / persist the state whether the DeviceKey has been set or not in the past. It should store the actual DeviceKey as well as the date+time of when it was last changed/set. Preferably the UserDefaults store - alike current settings store - should be used.

When a device key has been set in app it should be used for all Miataru client operations that support the DeviceKey. When those functions are being called and the server returns an error (because server side error OR when the device key is false) the app should handle this properly (make a plan how to implement to handle it and document behavior).

As initially no user has configured a DeviceKey (e.g. its not set) we firstly need to implement a view to set/view/update the new DeviceKey:

Place a new button on the iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView view that uses the key.card sfsymbol. When the button is tapped it presents a new view (as sheet) which offers the following information/functionality on display:

If a DeviceKey is not set yet: State (A)
If a DeviceKey is set: State (B)

View state (A) No DeviceKey set yet:
When no DeviceKey is set yet there should be a text explaining the meaning of the device key and the current state of „not set“. You should come up with a good explanation text helping the user to understand what the device key does and how it is important (e.g. protects any data write operations etc.). When set once it cannot be removed, only set to a different/new DeviceKey. If it is lost somehow the DeviceID cannot be updated/restored/becomes unusable and needs to be reset to a new DeviceID.

Below the explanation text there should be a button „generate and set DeviceKey“. When tapped the App should generate a UUID and use the MiataruClient to set this UUID as the new DeviceKey for the current device (setDeviceKey function). This new DeviceKey should properly persisted, including the current date/time.

The view should then update and show the state (B).

View state (B) When a DeviceKey has been successfully set on the server the view shows:
- the current DeviceKey (textbox) + copy-to-clipboard icon+functionality
- the time/date of the last update of the DeviceKey

A „regenerate/reset“ button:

When the regenerate/reset button is tapped a new DeviceKey is generated. The Miataru Client setDeviceKey function is called with the OLD DeviceKey and the NEW DeviceKey. When this is successful the new DeviceKey is persisted (+ time/date of setting).

A „restore“ button:

When the restore button is tapped a textbox entry opens with OK/cancel option. The user can paste / enter a previously saved DeviceKey from the clipboard or enter it with the keyboard. In order to check if the key is valid the app will try to call setDeviceKey with this user-provided-DeviceKey as the CurrentDeviceKey and NewDeviceKey. If it is valid the server will respond accordingly. If it is not, the server will also provide an error message and the app can handle this by showing the error message and re-opening the entry dialog with the previously user-entered-DeviceKey. The user can then either change the text and try again or cancel the process.

Make a thorough and holistic plan to implement this new behaviour and utilize this additional device key functionality.

Control tracking, data retention, server URL, device autolock, accuracy indicators, map type, zoom level, update interval, group zoom‑to‑fit, off‑screen arrows, auto‑refresh, reverse geocoding threshold, navigation mode, and route progress.\\\\\\\\n- View location tracking details or replay the onboarding wizard.\\\\\\\\n- Settings are grouped into tracking, app behavior, map configuration, and navigation sections for easier discovery.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- All app preferences are also available in the system Settings app.\\\\\\\\n- New options include: navigation route auto‑update, route progress visualization toggle, a global pulsing/shimmer switch for map markers, and off‑screen arrow visibility.\\\\\\\\n- Bicycle transport mode was removed; existing values fall back to walking for directions and car icons where applicable.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**For developers:**\\\\\\\\n- &#96;SettingsManager&#96; stores all preferences in &#96;UserDefaults&#96; and triggers side effects such as permission checks and auto‑refresh.\\\\\\\\n- &#96;iPhone_SettingsView&#96; binds directly to these properties and navigates to &#96;iPhone_LocationStatusView&#96; (now a page) or re-runs the onboarding flow via &#96;AppState&#96;.\\\\\\\\n- Defaults are registered from &#96;Settings.bundle&#96;, enabling control from the system Settings app. The manager observes low‑power state and scene phase for UI effect gating.\\\\\\\\n- Reverse geocoding threshold is user‑configurable (off/100 m/1 km/10 km; default 1 km) and applied centrally.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Location Status &amp; Error Handling\\\\\\\\n**For users:**\\\\\\\\n- A dedicated status view shows permission state, last GPS and server updates, background activity, and a log of recent events.\\\\\\\\n- If a network or permission error occurs, an overlay explains the problem.\\\\\\\\n- Map screens additionally display a network-error icon when the server cannot be reached.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- The status view lists speed and battery (when available) and tracks route‑request statistics over the last 24 hours.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**For developers:**\\\\\\\\n- &#96;LocationManager&#96; posts &#96;didSendOwnLocationUpdate&#96; notifications; &#96;ErrorOverlayManager&#96; and &#96;ErrorOverlay&#96; provide reusable alert UIs, and map views toggle a network icon via &#96;showNetworkErrorIcon&#96; flags.\\\\\\\\n- Status is presented as a dedicated page; related counters (e.g., daily route requests) are maintained in settings/state for self.devices.insert(myDevice, at: 0)\\\\\\\\n            debugLog(\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"[DEBUG] Eigenes Gerät mit DeviceID \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\(myDeviceID) wurde automatisch als erstes Device \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\(error)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\")\\\\\\\\n        }\\\\\\\\n        //print(\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Speichern ist temporär deaktiviert - muss repariert werden!!!\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\")\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n    private func load() -&gt; [KnownDevice] {\\\\\\\\n        guard let data = try? The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## App Navigation and Views\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n**For users:**\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. device ID as a QR code, copy it, or share via link or email.\\\\\\\\n- Add other devices by scanning their Miataru QR code.\\\\\\\\n- The QR tab offers one‑tap sharing, shows visitor history directly below your code, and the add‑device sheet guides scanning and rejects non‑Miataru codes.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- The share sheet includes additional options, and email sharing attaches the QR image reliably.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**For developers:**\\\\\\\\n- &#96;iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView&#96; renders customizable QR codes using the &#96;QRCode&#96; package and supports &#96;ShareLink&#96; and &#96;MFMailComposeViewController&#96;.\\\\\\\\n- &#96;VisitorHistoryViewModel&#96; and &#96;VisitorHistorySection&#96; power inline visitor history within the QR tab, while &#96;iPhone_VisitorHistoryView&#96; reuses the same data loader.\\\\\\\\n- &#96;iPhone_AddDeviceView&#96; validates the &#96;miataru://&#96; prefix from scanned codes before accepting an ID and allows manual entry with color selection.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Onboarding Flow\\\\\\\\n**For users:**\\\\\\\\n- A six‑step wizard guides through welcome, permissions, server URL, history settings, personal QR code display, and completion.\\\\\\\\n- Each step shows illustrations and contextual explanations; server selection validates custom HTTPS URLs, and completion flag controls whether the wizard reappears on next launch.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**For developers:**\\\\\\\\n- Platform‑specific containers (&#96;iPhone_OnboardingContainerView&#96;, &#96;iPad_OnboardingContainerView&#96;, &#96;Mac_OnboardingContainerView&#96;) embed the individual onboarding pages and update &#96;SettingsManager&#96; and &#96;UserDefaults.hasCompletedOnboarding&#96; as the user progresses.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Settings and Configuration\\\\\\\\n**For users:**\\\\\\\\n- Control tracking, data retention, server URL, device autolock, accuracy indicators, map type, zoom level, update interval, group zoom‑to‑fit, off‑screen arrows, auto‑refresh, reverse geocoding threshold, navigation mode, and route progress.\\\\\\\\n- View location tracking details or replay the onboarding Yes—**“no DeviceKey set” should continue to work as before**.

Why:
- `SettingsManager.deviceKey` defaults to `nil` when not set, so no key is sent. The setter also removes the key when empty.  
```96:114:/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/SettingsManagers/App Settings/SettingsManager.swift
    @Published var deviceKey: String? {
        didSet {
            if let key = deviceKey, !key.isEmpty {
                defaults.set(key, forKey: Keys.deviceKey)
            } else {
                defaults.removeObject(forKey: Keys.deviceKey)
            }
        }
    }
```

- UpdateLocation includes `DeviceKey: settings.deviceKey`, but the API client **only encodes it if it’s non-empty**, so when it’s nil/empty it’s omitted and behavior is unchanged.  
```383:393:/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/LocationManagers/LocationManager.swift
        return UpdateLocationPayload(
            Device: thisDeviceIDManager.shared.deviceID,
            DeviceKey: settings.deviceKey,
            Timestamp: String(Int64(timestamp)),
            Longitude: longitude,
            Latitude: latitude,
            HorizontalAccuracy: accuracy,
            Speed: speedValue,
            BatteryLevel: batteryPercent,
            Altitude: altitudeValue
        )
```
```255:268:/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/Libraries/MiataruClientSwift/Sources/MiataruAPIClient/MiataruAPIClient.swift
    public func encode(to encoder: Encoder) throws {
        var container = encoder.container(keyedBy: CodingKeys.self)
        try container.encode(Device, forKey: .Device)
        if let DeviceKey = DeviceKey, !DeviceKey.isEmpty {
            try container.encode(DeviceKey, forKey: .DeviceKey)
        }
        try container.encode(Timestamp, forKey: .Timestamp)
        // ...
    }
```

- Visitor history calls now pass the key too, but again it’s optional and only sent when present.  
```136:145:/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/LocationManagers/DeviceLocationRefresher.swift
            let visitors = try await MiataruAPIClient.getVisitorHistory(
                serverURL: serverURL,
                forDeviceID: currentDeviceID,
                deviceKey: settings.deviceKey,
                amount: 50
            )
```
```63:68:/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/views/iPhone/iPhone_VisitorHistoryView.swift
            let response = try await MiataruAPIClient.getVisitorHistoryWithConfig(
                serverURL: url,
                forDeviceID: ourDeviceId,
                deviceKey: settings.deviceKey,
                amount: nil
            )
```

Net effect: when no DeviceKey is set, requests behave exactly as before (no key sent). The only new behavior is that **if the server starts enforcing DeviceKey**, the auth handler triggers the sheet so the user can set or restore a key.

strings = data.get('strings', {})
missing = {}
for key, entry in strings.items():
    locs = entry.get('localizations', {})
    if not locs:
        continue
    if 'en' in locs:
        supported = {'da','de','en','es','fi','fr','it','ja','nl','zh-Hans'}
        missing_langs = sorted(supported - set(locs.keys()))
        if missing_langs:
            missing[key] = missing_langs

for key, langs in sorted(missing.items()):
    if key.startswith('device_key_') or key in {'close_button_label','cancel_button_label'}:
        print(key, ':', ','.join(langs))

import json
from pathlib import Path

path = Path('/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/Assets/Localizable.xcstrings')
with path.open('r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

strings = data.setdefault('strings', {})
key = 'device_key_restore_server_error'
entry = strings.get(key)
if not entry:
    entry = {
        'comment': 'Server rejected DeviceKey during restore',
        'localizations': {
            'en': {'stringUnit': {'state': 'translated', 'value': 'The server did not accept this DeviceKey, try again!'}},
        },
    }
    strings[key] = entry

translations = {
    'da': 'Serveren accepterede ikke denne DeviceKey, prøv igen!',
    'de': 'Der Server hat diesen DeviceKey nicht akzeptiert, bitte erneut versuchen!',
    'es': 'El servidor no aceptó este DeviceKey, ¡inténtalo de nuevo!',
    'fi': 'Palvelin ei hyväksynyt tätä DeviceKeytä, yritä uudelleen!',
    'fr': 'Le serveur n’a pas accepté ce DeviceKey, réessaie !',
    'it': 'Il server non ha accettato questo DeviceKey, riprova!',
    'ja': 'サーバーがこの DeviceKey を受け付けませんでした。もう一度お試しください。',
    'nl': 'De server heeft deze DeviceKey niet geaccepteerd, probeer het opnieuw!',
    'zh-Hans': '服务器未接受此 DeviceKey，请重试！',
}
locs = entry.setdefault('localizations', {})
for lang, value in translations.items():
    if lang not in locs:
        locs[lang] = {'stringUnit': {'state': 'translated', 'value': value}}

with path.open('w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    json.dump(data, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
    f.write('\n')
PY

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
**Planning auth error handling**

I'm adding a deviceKeyAuthBlocked flag in SettingsManager set by LocationManager on auth errors to stop location updates until user relaunches and resets the key. I'll ensure LocationManager checks this flag before sending updates and clears it on app activation if the key changes, persisting the flag in UserDefaults. Banner display will trigger only when active, and error handling will update tracking and server status accordingly.
**Refining tracking block logic**

I'm implementing deviceKeyAuthBlocked and deviceKeyAuthBlockedKey in SettingsManager to track auth errors and block updates until the device key resets on app launch. LocationManager will stop tracking on block, skip sending updates while blocked, and auto-restart tracking on app activation if unblocked and user preferences allow. Banner display triggers on app launch if blocked. The block guards startTracking and observing settings to prevent unwanted updates while blocked.</details></think>

Made the DeviceKey mismatch stop all location updates until the app is relaunched **and** the key is changed to a working one, and ensured the user sees a banner message on app launch.

What changed:
- **Stop updates on mismatch**: When UpdateLocation fails due to DeviceKey mismatch, tracking stops and a `deviceKeyAuthBlocked` flag is persisted.
- **No retries while blocked**: `startTracking` and `sendLocationToServer` bail out while blocked.
- **Auto-resume after key reset**: Changing the DeviceKey clears the block; when the app becomes active, tracking restarts if allowed.
- **Visible message on launch**: Root views now show the mismatch banner on app start if blocked, so the user sees it immediately.

If you want the sheet to auto-open on launch (not just the banner), I can add that too.

_**User**_

---

_**Agent (model gpt-5.2-codex, mode Agent)**_

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
**Clarifying deviceKey reset logic**

The deviceKey resets only if deviceKeyAuthBlocked is true, a blocked key exists, and the current key differs from the blocked key, ensuring same keys don't clear. If a restored key differs, reset happens to handle mismatch between client and server keys.</details></think>

---

Yes, it’s reset when the key changes to a different value. In `SettingsManager.deviceKey`’s `didSet`, if `deviceKeyAuthBlocked` is true **and** the new key differs from the blocked key, the block is cleared and the blocked key is removed. That means:

- If the user **sets/restores a different (working) key**, the block clears.
- If they **re‑set the same key** that was blocked, it will **not** clear.

If you want it to clear after a successful restore even when the key is the same (for cases where the server was fixed), I can adjust that logic.

Fixed the Miataru client so server errors (like the 403 DeviceKey mismatch) aren’t incorrectly wrapped as `encodingError`. The issue was in `performPostRequest(url:jsonPayload:)` catching *all* errors and rethrowing as `encodingError`, which masked `APIError.serverError`. Now `APIError` is rethrown directly, so mismatch detection will work and the app will stop updates + show the banner/sheet.

This should address the log line:
```
[MiataruAPIClient] Failed to encode request ...
```
which was misleading for server errors.

If you want, I can also suppress the “Location update accepted” debug log to avoid confusion (that line is about GPS acceptance, not server acceptance).
